source_text.GitHub issue #4: Title: 'Add KZ translation'. Body: 'Add KZ translation'

task.description:
GitHub issue #4 ('Add KZ translation') asks for a Kazakh version of the site. This is structurally identical to GitHub issue #3 ('translate to en'), which this project just resolved via REQ-003 (routing/mechanism, owner FRONTEND-DEV) + REQ-004 (real translations, owner CONTENT-BA, depends_on REQ-003) -- read both of those entries in docs/agents/requirements.yaml directly as your primary precedent/template, plus docs/agents/decisions/0002-content-ba-owns-message-catalogs.md.

Current state (verify yourself, don't trust this summary): src/i18n/routing.ts has locales=['ru','uz','en'], defaultLocale='ru'. No 'kk' (Kazakh) locale exists anywhere. messages/ru.json, messages/uz.json, messages/en.json all exist with matching key sets (177 keys as of REQ-004's close, but re-verify the current count -- it may have grown). src/components/landing/LocaleSwitcher.tsx iterates routing.locales generically (confirmed in REQ-003's design/build), so adding a locale to the array is expected to be sufficient for the switcher UI, same as REQ-003 found -- but verify this claim still holds by reading the file yourself rather than assuming it's unchanged. The design system readme's brand voice principle #6 already commits to 'Multilingual by default -- Russian, Uzbek, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Tajik, English -- equal weight' (content_ba_guide.md, design system readme), so Kazakh is a locale this project already committed to, not new scope invention.

Use ISO locale code 'kk' for Kazakh (the standard ISO 639-1 code; next-intl and Next.js both expect ISO codes, matching how 'ru'/'uz'/'en' are already used). State this choice explicitly rather than silently assuming it.

Draft this as two requirements sized to one agent turn each, mirroring REQ-003/REQ-004's split exactly:
1. FRONTEND-DEV-owned requirement: add 'kk' to routing.ts's locales array, defaultLocale stays 'ru' unless you find a stated reason to change it (there isn't one -- state this explicitly, don't silently imply a change), seed messages/kk.json with every current messages/ru.json key duplicated verbatim as a placeholder. Verify LocaleSwitcher.tsx/request.ts/layout.tsx still need no code change (or state what changed if they do).
2. CONTENT-BA-owned requirement, depends_on the first: write real Kazakh (Latin or Cyrillic script -- state which and why; note Kazakh has historically used Cyrillic script and the ru/uz precedent in this project used Latin script for Uzbek specifically because that's Uzbekistan's current official script -- Kazakhstan's ongoing Latin transition is not complete, so don't assume Latin without justifying it) copy for every messages/kk.json key, following content_ba_guide.md's rules and restating the domain-vocabulary decision for this locale (should follow the same verbatim-English-domain-terms precedent as REQ-002/REQ-004 unless you find a reason it doesn't apply).

Read docs/agents/requirements.yaml in full first (existing schema + REQ-001a/b/REQ-002/REQ-003/REQ-004 as direct precedent). Read docs/agents/anti-patterns.md and docs/agents/decisions/ for anything relevant.
acceptance_criteria: Two new entries appended to docs/agents/requirements.yaml (next sequential ids after REQ-004), following the exact existing schema, status: pending
The second requirement's depends_on includes the first
Each requirement has >=2 concrete, testable acceptance criteria (script/diff/grep/build-output verifiable, no vague language)
The requirement(s) state explicitly what defaultLocale remains and why
The ISO locale code choice ('kk') is stated explicitly with reasoning
The script decision (Cyrillic vs Latin) for Kazakh copy is stated explicitly with reasoning, not silently assumed from the Uzbek precedent
The domain-vocabulary-in-Kazakh decision is stated explicitly, citing whether it follows or diverges from the REQ-002/REQ-004 precedent and why
Neither requirement contradicts any existing done requirement's description
Sized to one agent turn per requirement per WF-01 Step 1c, following the REQ-003/REQ-004 precedent split
